title: Jump Game V
notes:
## Intuition

Every jump lands on a strictly lower value, so no journey can return to an index. That makes `dp[i]`, the most indices visited when starting at `i`, well defined: `dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j])` over the indices `j` reachable from `i`. Each such `j` is lower than `i`, so filling `dp` from the lowest value to the highest means every `dp[j]` is final when it is needed.

## Approach

1. Sort the indices by `arr` value into `order`, and start every `dp[i]` at `1` (the start index alone).
2. Take indices in that order. For each `i`, walk left over at most `d` positions.
3. Stop at the first `j` with `arr[j] >= arr[i]`, which blocks everything beyond it. Each lower `j` before it is reachable: update `dp[i]` with `dp[j] + 1`.
4. Walk right in the same way.
5. Track `best`, the largest `dp[i]`, and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [6,4,14,6,8,13,9,7,10,6,12]`, `d = 2`. Sorting by value finishes the indices in the order `1, 0, 3, 9, 7, 4, 6, 8, 10, 5, 2`.

- Index 7 (value `7`) is boxed in by `9` on the left and `10` on the right, so `dp[7] = 1`.
- Index 6 (`9`) is blocked on the left by `13` but can drop to index 7, so `dp[6] = 2`.
- Index 8 (`10`) reaches index 7 and, over it, index 6, so `dp[8] = dp[6] + 1 = 3`.
- Index 10 (`12`) reaches index 9 (`dp 1`) and index 8 (`dp 3`), so `dp[10] = 4`.

No other index does better (`dp[5]` and `dp[2]` are `3`), so the answer is `4`, the journey 10 → 8 → 6 → 7.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n + n·d): one sort, then at most `2d` neighbours per index.
- Space: O(n) for `order` and `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- An equal value also blocks: the tests are `arr[j] >= arr[i]` to stop and strictly lower to jump.
- Once a blocker is met, stop the walk on that side; indices beyond it are unreachable even if they are lower.
- Processing indices left to right is wrong: `dp[j]` for a lower neighbour on the right would not be ready. Sort by value first.
- The answer counts indices, so a lone index (or all-equal values) gives `1`, not `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `arr` |
| `order` | indices sorted from lowest to highest value |
| `dp` | `dp[i]` is the most indices visited starting at `i` |
| `best` | the largest `dp[i]` so far |
| `i` | the index being finished |
| `j` | a neighbour within `d` steps of `i` |

narration.7: Finish the indices in increasing order of value.
narration.8: Walk left from i, at most d positions.
narration.9: A value at least as high as arr[i] blocks this jump and every jump past it.
